questions.q: By default, how long before a Salesforce password expires?
options: 30 days
60 days
90 days
180 days
questions.explain: The default User passwords expire in setting is 90 days, though it's configurable org-wide and per profile.

questions.q: What does Enforce password history control by default?
options: How long a password stays valid before expiring
How many previous passwords can't be immediately reused (3 by default)
How many failed login attempts are allowed
Whether a password question is required
questions.explain: Password history remembers a number of previous passwords (3 by default) so users can't just cycle back to an old one.

questions.q: What does the Session Settings Timeout Value actually control?
options: How long before a password must be changed
How many failed logins trigger a lockout
How long a session stays active during inactivity before the user is logged out
How long a locked-out account stays locked
questions.explain: Timeout Value is about an already-logged-in session — how long it can sit idle before Salesforce ends it, independent of password rules.

questions.q: Where in Setup do both Password Policies and Session Settings live?
options: Company Information
The Security Controls menu
Object Manager
App Manager
questions.explain: Both pages sit in the Security Controls section of Setup, one Quick Find search away.

questions.q: What happens when Password Policies or Session Settings are set at the profile level?
options: Profile-level settings are ignored in favor of org-wide defaults
Profile-level settings override the org-wide defaults for that profile's users
Profile-level settings only apply to System Administrators
Profile-level settings require a separate Session Settings license
questions.explain: Just like Login Hours and Login IP Ranges from the previous lesson, profile-level password and session settings take precedence over the org-wide defaults for users on that profile.
